passages.say: The question of whether students should be allowed to use phones in class has divided opinion. Supporters argue that phones, if used wisely, provide instant access to information. Critics, on the other hand, point out that notifications distract students from learning. Perhaps the answer lies in teaching students to use technology responsibly.

passages.say: In 2020, Singapore's hawker culture was inscribed on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage. For many Singaporeans, hawker centres are more than places to eat; they are spaces where people of all backgrounds gather. Yet the trade faces a challenge, as fewer young people are willing to take over stalls from their ageing owners. Unless new hawkers are found, some beloved dishes may disappear.

passages.say: Last December, our school sent a group of students to help build a library in a rural village. Before the trip, I had assumed that we would be the ones teaching the villagers. In reality, they taught us far more about resourcefulness and community. Living without air-conditioning and fast internet was difficult at first, but I soon stopped missing them. The experience changed the way I look at the world.
